reason: The text portrays Nehemiah as a leader who consistently demonstrates care for the welfare of the regular people through multiple concrete actions: he organizes the people for both work and defense while ensuring their safety (מִשְׁמָר יוֹמָ֥ם וָלַ֖יְלָה - guard duty day and night), provides emotional and spiritual encouragement to address their fears (אַל־ תִּֽירְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם - 'do not be afraid'), establishes practical work schedules that allow for rest and sleep (יָלִ֖ינוּ בְּת֣וֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם - 'lodge in Jerusalem'), and organizes the population by families with protective resources. The passage emphasizes that Nehemiah personally oversees these arrangements and participates in the burden alongside the people, exemplifying a model of leadership centered on protecting and managing the welfare of the common population.
